direction: Improve `score_ruin_nodes` by making the ruin priority a stagnation-adaptive, rank-power-mixed score: multiply normalized removal savings by (a) a tight-capacity load gate that favours customers on near-full routes (weakest regime = capacity_level tight, gap -23.6%), (b) an eccentric-depot radial gate that favours extreme-radius customers (weakest regime = depot_style eccentric, gap -21.0%), and (c) blend with a Shaw-style spatial-cluster relatedness term when stagnation_ratio grows, so destroy sets shift from "worst-cost" (early, iter_frac<0.3) to "related cluster + high-load" (late, stagnating). Rank-power exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) interpolates from p≈1.0 early to p≈3.0 under stagnation, with deterministic index-based tie-breaking.

operations.mechanism: KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the single evolvable hook score_ruin_nodes with the multiplicative gate + rank-power form (score = rank_power(|savings|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio))) and shows an evolved version beating the zero-evolution Worst-Cost control (23.3186 vs 23.3474) at 500 ms, with first_feasible_ms ~2-3 ms so budget exhaustion is not a risk here. The only evolvable surface is this hook; postprocess must remain 'none'. This round's delta is therefore to push the two gates and the rank-power exponent toward the archive's identified weak regimes (tight capacity, eccentric depot, clustered spatial) and to add a Shaw-relatedness diversification term driven by stagnation_ratio, which KB method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret identifies as the standard complement to worst-removal. Direction stays strictly inside the anytime-LNS skeleton contract: single hook, read-only state inputs, deterministic tie-breaking, no RNG.
